results.label: the ACTUAL 145-file M109 parent is the previous milestone: one symmetric number applied by Math.abs, echoed as ?window=5 and as the 45 default, with no columns and no split
the parent’s own source is the recorded defect, read on the parent tree: one windowMin constant and one Math.abs test for both sides of a release
the parent produced owned history to inherit: three closed trades and one account row
the parent’s own restart lazily creates its M102 default strategy snapshot and moves sqlite_sequence — recorded as inherited parent behaviour and isolated, not merged into the delta
M110 adds exactly TWO columns to `accounts` — the asymmetric pair — and no other schema object appears, disappears or changes
both columns are added NOT NULL with the documented defaults, and each carries its own CHECK in the stored schema text
every pre-existing account column keeps its name, declared type, nullability and default, and the two new columns are appended LAST
the parent’s account row carried NO news key at all — its single number lived in the engine, not in the database
no view or trigger anywhere in the upgraded schema mentions the old single knob, and the only object whose text mentions the pair is `accounts`
the inherited account reads at the documented 15/45 — the parent’s own 45 constant did NOT become the pre-release block, and 45/45 did NOT survive
every inherited fact outside `accounts` is byte-identical after the upgrade: trades, gate answers, intention, practice and the session rows
the ONLY difference in the inherited `accounts` rows is the two new columns — id, name, balance and policy fields are untouched
the upgraded tree reads the inherited account through its OWN API at 15/45, with no bare `window_min` anywhere in the row or the payload
its news payload carries the resolved pair (before/after + provenance), not the parent’s single knob
the upgraded `/accounts` row carries exactly the two news keys and nothing else news-shaped
the parent’s own `?window=` call — which worked on this very database minutes earlier — is now a 400 `news_window_split_required`, and so is `?window_min=`
a settle under the floor is refused on the inherited database (400 `news_settle_below_floor`), a legal settle is accepted, and a research pair is applied per request
hostile values written straight to SQLite are refused by the columns themselves: 0 and 241 out of the block’s bounds, a fractional 1.5 and a word on the block, and 0, 29, 241 and 30.5 on the settle
a news read on the inherited database writes nothing at all: every table byte-identical, no object added
a bundle from the parent era (no news keys at all) imports its trades onto this desk and cannot move the pair
a hostile bundle carrying its own news numbers in the account row AND at the root of the file imports its trade but leaves both clocks at the stored 15/45, creating no account
an accepted account write answers with a structured `news_note` naming the pair it stored and its own bounds
explicitly null or blank news values are refused (`news_window_invalid`) rather than coerced to a default, and the stored pair does not move
the columns accept their own boundary values — block 1 and 240, settle 30 and 240 — each written and read back exactly
a per-request research pair (`?before=60&after=120`) is answered but NOT stored: the account still reads 15/45 afterwards
recording a trade (200) adds one row and does not touch the news pair or any other accounts fact
the export carries both columns and NO key spelling the old single number, so a backup taken on the upgraded tree can be restored without inventing one
after the whole battery the news endpoint still reads the same stored pair, and the pair is the one the trader set
a fresh database gets the SAME two definitions (type, NOT NULL, default) — and the same CHECKs — as an upgraded one, re-created from the DDL rather than inherited
and the position difference is recorded instead of hidden: the inherited columns are appended LAST, the fresh DDL places them before the drawdown fields
a brand-new delivered database reads its own account at 15/45 with no bare `window_min` column anywhere in the schema
a second open of the upgraded database is a no-op: same objects, same columns, same pair, same facts
the change is additive in the strongest sense available here: the PARENT’s own code still reads the upgraded file and finds its history intact

scope: ACTUAL145-file M109 release parent → delivered tree on the same database: exactly two added columns with their own CHECKs, every other schema object and inherited fact byte-identical, the parent’s single knob refused rather than mapped, re-open a no-op; synthetic/local, not broker/real-money proof
